title: LectureQ: catch the questions you have mid-lecture, for Mac, iPhone and iPad
description: Jot down a question with one shortcut mid-lecture. It sits beside your notes from that moment until you answer it. Free for up to 10 lectures.

hero.headline:
Don't let a mid-lecture
question slip away
hero.lead: Press `⌘⇧N`, type one line, and the question lands beside your notes from that minute. Keep listening. Find the answer later.
hero.cta: Get it free on the App Store
hero.note: For Mac (macOS 14 or later), iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 or later). No account; syncs through your own iCloud.

demo.title: Try it here

demo.note: This demo follows the same rules as the app. Nothing you type here is saved anywhere.

Large learning rate η diverges, small one is too slow

problem.title: When the lecture ends, do you still remember the question?
problem.text: The moment you think "wait, why?" the lecturer has already moved on. The question mark in the margin loses track of which explanation it came from, and it never gets answered. LectureQ pins each question to your notes from that moment and keeps it in front of you until you've worked it out.

features.title: Ask without missing the next sentence
features.text:
Open the input window with `Add Question` in the toolbar or `⌘⇧N`. The time fills in for you. `Return` saves, and `⌘Return` saves and gets you ready for the next one.
Each question shows up as a ? beside the time block it belongs to, so later you can see exactly which part of the lecture it came from.

features.title: Answered questions become what you learned
features.text:
Write the answer in your own words, mark it resolved, and it joins What I Learned in the summary. Anything still open stays under Questions to Ask, so your list for the next class builds itself.
`Copy AI Prompt` in the question details puts a ready-made prompt on the clipboard, filled in with the lecture name and your notes from that moment. Paste it into whichever AI service you already use.

features.title: See where your thinking went
features.text:
Follow-up questions stack indented under the question they came from, and the graph links them with arrows. Click a node to jump straight to that question.
In Learning Status you can write down where you are now, where you want to be when the course ends, and what you want to learn, then compare.

items.title: Create a lecture
items.text: Add one from the lecture menu at the left of the toolbar, or import a conversation saved as Markdown.

items.title: Write it down as it comes
items.text: Press `⌘⇧N`. One line is enough, and the time is filled in.

items.title: Answer it later
items.text: Write the answer and click the ? to mark it resolved. It moves to What I Learned.

items.q: What do the colors of the ? mean?
items.a: In the list, an empty orange circle is a question you haven't resolved yet and a filled green one is resolved. Click the ? to switch between them, and turn on `Unresolved Only` in the toolbar to see only open questions. Beside a time block, the color shows whether it's resolved and a filled circle means an answer has been written.

Click `Add Block` and a new block starts at that moment, while the previous one is trimmed to end there. If you add a question at a time no block covers, a block is created around it for you. Use `Settings` at the top right of a block to change its color, start time and length, or delete it. Once you delete a block yourself, that lecture stops creating blocks automatically.

items.q: What's the difference between Resolved and What I Learned?
items.a: When you tick `Resolved` in the question details, you can also choose whether it counts toward What I Learned. Only resolved questions you've included appear there. You can also exclude or re-add them from the summary, and the answer stays put either way.

items.q: How do the AI prompts work?
items.a: In the question details, open `Copy AI Prompt` next to Answer and pick a step: Refine the Question, Find the Answer, Question the Answer, Draw Out Follow-ups or Get My Answer Graded. A prompt filled in with the lecture name, your notes from that moment, your learning status and the original question is copied to the clipboard. The prompt text itself is currently in Korean; most AI services will still understand it, and you can ask for the reply in English. Get My Answer Graded needs your own answer in the Answer field first. The app never talks to an AI service itself.

items.q: Can I import a conversation saved as Markdown?
items.a: Choose `Import from Markdown…` in the lecture menu. `# Title` becomes the lecture name, and in each `## Section` the first question is the original question and the ones after it are follow-ups. Lines from the first speaker in the file become questions, and lines from anyone else become the answer to the question just before. The original file is never changed.

items.q: How do I delete a question or a lecture?
items.a: Right-click a question in the list and choose `Delete`. For a lecture, use `Delete Current Lecture` in the lecture menu; its questions and blocks go with it. This can't be undone, so back up anything important first.

items.q: Where is my data stored, and how do I back it up?
items.a: Everything is stored on your device and, if you’re signed in to iCloud, synced between your own Mac, iPhone and iPad through your iCloud. The developer can’t see it. To back up on a Mac, quit the app and copy the whole folder ~/Library/Containers/com.lectureq.LectureQ/Data/Library/Application Support/LectureQ/ including the -wal and -shm files. The app only sends anonymous usage statistics, such as the app version and the days it was opened, never what you write.
Use `⌘+` to make it bigger, `⌘-` to make it smaller and `⌘0` to reset. It goes from 85% to 200% and remembers your setting.

items.q: Which devices does it run on?
items.a: Any Mac with macOS 14 or later, and iPhone and iPad with iOS or iPadOS 18 or later. The source code is public on GitHub at M1zz/LectureQ.

items.q: Something isn't working. Who do I tell?
items.a: Send feedback from Settings (`⌘,`) in the app, or email the address below. Include your macOS version and what you were doing when it happened, and we can look into it faster.
